page: Microsoft Azure F8als_v6 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 8 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, which classifies it as a low-memory, compute-focused configuration. It lacks local storage and GPUs but supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing is a notable strength, ranking in the top 10% of Geekbench tests. Multi-core performance, static web serving, and Redis operations fall within average ranges. However, a key performance tradeoff is uncached large-block read memory bandwidth, which registers in the bottom 25%.

Given its compute-heavy, low-memory profile, the F8als_v6 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high single-thread CPU performance without massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for text processing, software compilation, lightweight web serving, and small-scale LLM text generation. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-block data streaming due to its memory bandwidth constraints and 16 GB RAM limit.
